options: It trains a new model from scratch
It files a run's model artifact under a registered model name, creating the next auto-incrementing version
It permanently deletes older versions of a model
It deploys the model directly to a production server
questions.explain: register_model takes an artifact URI from a specific run and registers it under a named model, auto-incrementing the version number each time.

questions.q: Why has MLflow deprecated the stage-based lifecycle (None/Staging/Production/Archived)?
options: Because stages were too slow to query
Because stage is a property of the version, so only one version can hold a given stage registry-wide, and "production" means something different per team
Because MLflow no longer supports Python
Because stages could not be set through the API, only the UI
questions.explain: Stage is tied to the version itself, creating a structural bottleneck and inconsistent meaning across teams — aliases and tags replace it.

questions.q: What is a model registry alias, such as "champion"?
options: A permanent, unchangeable label burned into the model file
A mutable, named pointer to a specific model version that a serving job resolves at load time
A synonym for the model's registered name
A required field when logging any metric
questions.explain: An alias like "champion" points to whichever version currently holds that role. Promoting a new model means moving the pointer, not touching the model or anything downstream of it.

questions.q: In the current recommended MLflow pattern, what is the role of a tag (e.g. set_model_version_tag)?
options: To control which version is currently serving production traffic
To carry free-form metadata (like a git commit hash or who validated it), separate from lifecycle state
To permanently archive a model version
To rename the registered model
questions.explain: Tags carry metadata; aliases now handle the lifecycle role that stages used to try to do at the same time.

questions.q: In Weights & Biases, how does a logged artifact become part of the Model Registry?
options: It happens automatically the moment wandb.init() is called
By explicitly linking the artifact into the registry with a call like run.link_artifact()
By renaming the artifact file on disk
W&B does not have a model registry concept
questions.explain: W&B separates a logged artifact from a registry entry; link_artifact() is the explicit step that connects a specific artifact version into a named registry entry.
